hook: Your body decides something is wrong before your mind has finished reading the room.
topic: Why the body reacts before the brain catches up
body:
**Your body decided something was wrong before your brain even registered what happened.**

Your chest tightened. Your heart rate climbed. Your thoughts started accelerating toward the exits.

And then your rational mind arrived at the scene, looked around, and found nothing. No threat. No fire. Nothing that justified what your body was already doing.

And yet the body continued.

This isn't a malfunction. Your brain runs two processing pathways simultaneously — and the one connected to threat response is faster than conscious thought. It was built to be. It doesn't wait for your assessment because, evolutionarily, waiting got you killed.

So when you're standing there, fully aware that you're probably fine, completely unable to make the feeling stop — that's not a broken nervous system. That is a very fast one.

The problem isn't the speed. The problem is that it misfires. And misfiring is something you can actually work with.

Next time your body fires first, don't argue with the feeling. That's the wrong tool. Your body has a different entry point — and that's where the interrupt has to start.

I broke down the full three-step protocol in the guide linked in my bio — it's free.
